comparison: Perfect agreement on hypothalamus results at 200 µm depth (C81-C84). Both find claims supported. OpenEval notes the 'slight reduction' is not precisely quantified, while peer reviewers accept the demonstration without concerns.

Perfect agreement on cortical cell type identification (C78-C80). Both find claims supported. OpenEval notes this validates known biology rather than providing novel insights and questions the 'all previously known subclasses' claim, while peer reviewers accept without qualification.

Perfect agreement on interneuron pairing analysis (C85-C91). Both find claims supported. OpenEval notes the gap junction hypothesis (C86) is cited speculation not tested here, while peer reviewers accept the findings without raising this concern.

Perfect agreement on regional differences in interneuron organization (C92-C97). Both find claims supported. OpenEval appreciates the cautious interpretation acknowledging confounding factors (C97), and peer reviewers accept the conclusions without concerns.

Strong agreement on validation results and quality assessment (C64-C72, C77). Both find claims supported. OpenEval notes the interpretation about complete cell capture (C72) is somewhat speculative and that advantages of thick-tissue imaging (C73-C77) are logical but not directly tested, while peer reviewers find evidence 'solid and compelling' without these qualifications.

Strong agreement on protocol optimization (C52-C63). Both find claims supported. OpenEval notes the lack of direct before/after comparisons quantifying individual optimization contributions, while peer reviewers explicitly praise 'extensive protocol optimization' without this concern.

Divergent evaluations of future applications (C112-C117, C120). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative future applications not experimentally validated. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the potential applications and noting 'major impact on future spatial transcriptomics studies.'

Strong agreement on deep learning approach for detection efficiency recovery (C31-C37, C124-C125). Both find claims supported. OpenEval notes generalizability to different tissue types or imaging conditions is not tested, while peer reviewers accept the approach without raising this limitation.

Agreement on water-immersion objective performance (C43-C46). Both find claims supported. OpenEval notes direct quantitative comparison of oil vs water objectives on the same sample is not shown, while peer reviewers find methods 'sufficiently detailed' without this concern.

Agreement on overall technical advance (C3-C5, C98, C108-C111). Both find the method represents a major technical advance. OpenEval notes C111 is speculative extrapolation and lacks direct experimental comparison with other methods, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'a major technical advance' and 'important technical method paper' without these qualifications.

Partial overlap on methodological accessibility (C118-C119). Both find claims supported. OpenEval evaluates these as straightforward methodological claims supporting reproducibility. Peer reviewers include these in broader assessment of the work's accessibility and impact (C120).

OpenEval evaluated background and motivation claims (C1-C2, C6-C24) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations, noting C18 is somewhat speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluated literature positioning and comparison claims (C99-C107) as SUPPORTED, noting fair discussion of tradeoffs but lack of direct experimental comparison with alternative methods. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these comparative claims.
